subject: science
passage: The gharial, a crocodilian found in rivers of India and Nepal, has a snout so long and narrow that it can look almost fragile. That shape, however, is well suited to the gharial's diet, which consists mainly of fish. A slender snout meets little resistance from the water, so the animal can swing its head sideways quickly to snap up its prey. The same specialization carries a cost: because the gharial depends so heavily on fish, it struggles wherever river fish become scarce.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that the gharial's snout makes it a weaker hunter than other crocodilians
choices.B: To describe the rivers of India and Nepal where gharials are found
choices.C: To explain how a feature of the gharial suits its diet and why that feature also leaves it vulnerable
choices.D: To explain why fish in the rivers of India and Nepal have become scarce

explanation.why: The text first explains that the narrow snout, though it looks "fragile," helps the gharial catch fish quickly. The final sentence adds a qualification: "The same specialization carries a cost," since the animal suffers when fish are scarce. The purpose covers both the advantage and the drawback.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the snout is "well suited" to catching fish, and it never compares the gharial with other crocodilians.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The rivers are mentioned only to say where gharials live; they are not the focus.
explanation.C: Correct. The text explains how the snout helps the gharial catch fish and then how dependence on fish makes it vulnerable.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text mentions places where fish become scarce but never explains why that happens.
